reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is an instructional walkthrough of creating, verifying, and preparing a YouTube channel for AdSense monetization, showing platform setup steps and review requirements. Although it discusses selecting India and demonstrates a fake address, the available video evidence says there is no evidence that false information was submitted, viewers were solicited to pay, or verification or payment occurred.

opening.argument: Judge, the income pitch is tied to actions the viewer is asked to take. The speaker introduces the video as a way to earn from a YouTube channel, then asks interested viewers to subscribe and follow the linked earlier videos. More importantly, the walkthrough directs them into AdSense sign-up as part of the earning process. The question is not whether creating a channel costs money; it is whether the presentation draws viewers into an account-creation flow with earnings as the incentive.

citations.quote: In today's video I am going to tell you how to earn money from youtube channel
If you are interested, please subscribe to this channel and like this video
I have put the link in the description click that link and watch that video
Next process will be sign up for AdSense

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's channel-creation and verification steps explain how the pitch is delivered, but they do not sever the connection between those steps and the promised earning opportunity. Nor does the absence of a payment request settle whether viewers are being solicited to enter an income-oriented sign-up flow. The speaker expressly connects monetization to additional money; the review threshold limits when that money might arrive, not why viewers are guided through the setup.

citations.quote: And by this,your monetization program gets you an additional money

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These quotes show a conventional creator tutorial and a request to subscribe to the tutorial channel, not an unusually easy cash claim. The demonstrated pathway remains conditional: the speaker says viewers need watch hours and subscribers and that YouTube will review the channel. AdSense sign-up is presented as a step in that platform process, not as a claim that signing up itself pays.

citations.quote: you have to create watch hours 4000 hours from another day of 12 months period till that day you have a 4000 hours watch time in a plus channel of 1000 subscriber
And then, YouTube will review your monetization program

opening.argument: Judge, examine the earning setup at its most troubling points. The speaker says a Nepal-based channel should select India as its country and reports that a previously unavailable monetization option then appears. The AdSense walkthrough also includes an address the speaker calls fake. Even allowing for the stated demo context, those choices put inaccurate account information adjacent to an income-enabling process. That combination warrants more concern than the ordinary setup screens alone suggest.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the cited material does not prove a false address was accepted or a payment occurred. But its account of routine setup omits the speaker's stated reason for changing the country setting: the monetization option was initially unavailable and appeared afterward. A completed payout is not necessary to assess the risk in an income-oriented walkthrough that presents this setting change as a route to the option.

citations.quote: It was not eligible at first But now it has been enabled now we can see it is not usable but now we got monetization enable option

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An available option is not monetization or earnings. The speaker immediately says monetization cannot yet be enabled, and the later screen still shows zero watch hours and zero subscribers toward review. The address is explicitly described as a demo, while the guidance to viewers calls for an exact address matching their documents. These facts do not establish a deceptive reward or a successful bypass.

opening.argument: Judge, this walkthrough also promotes continued participation in the speaker's earning-focused channel. Viewers are directed to earlier linked videos, asked to subscribe, and told that further videos will address reaching subscribers and views. Those invitations sit inside the promise of learning to earn online. The operational demonstration makes the invitation more credible, but it should not make the promotional function disappear: the speaker is building an audience around an income pathway and asking viewers to follow along.

citations.quote: I will guide you how to earn money from online
If you have not seen the previous videos I have put the link in the description click that link and watch that video
And now let me tell you about how to do video upload, how to reach subscribers, how to have views for your viewers, I will post those information down below.
If you are very interested do subscribe to this channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense identifies genuine instructional content, but instruction and promotion can coexist. The opening focuses on the platform steps while leaving out the repeated invitations to consume more of the speaker's income-related content. The absence of a viewer payment or completed verification narrows what can be alleged; it does not erase the speaker's effort to convert the earnings topic into subscriptions and further viewing.

citations.quote: If you are very interested do subscribe to this channel.
If you have not seen the previous videos I have put the link in the description click that link and watch that video

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Requests to watch related tutorials and subscribe do not turn a platform walkthrough into a scam. The speaker describes creating and customizing a channel, and expressly leaves uploading for a later video. More decisively, the earning pathway is subject to watch-time and subscriber requirements followed by review. The prosecution identifies channel promotion, but not a deceptive or unusually easy reward tied to those requests.
